聞.meaning: A castle <part>gate</part> has no bell and no knocker, just a huge stone <part>ear</part> carved in the middle. Whisper your name into it and the doors creak open; mumble, and nothing happens. It only lets in those it can <kanji>hear</kanji>.
聞.on: A ba<sound>boon</sound> bellows its name into the stone ear so loudly that the doors fly open and knock it flat.
聞.kun: If the ear won't hear you, there's always the spare <sound>key</sound> under the doormat.

期.meaning: On a <part>bookshelf</part> sits a row of diaries, one for each <part>moon</part>: a new full moon, a new book. When the last page is full, it goes back on the shelf and the next one starts. Each book holds one <kanji>period</kanji> of time.
期.on: Each diary has a tiny brass lock, and the only <sound>key</sound> hangs round your neck.

到.meaning: A messenger gallops into town with a letter speared on a <part>dagger</part> and jams it into the wooden <part>podium</part> with a thunk. Everyone looks up. He's here at last! Ring the bells for his <kanji>arrival</kanji>.
到.on: He leaps off his horse and lands right on the mayor's <sound>toe</sound>.
到.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals the mayor, hopping into a <sound>tu</sound>b of cold water to soothe her foot.

秋.meaning: A scarecrow stuffed with <part>grain</part> stalks shivers in the first chilly wind, so the farmer lights a small <part>fire</part> at his feet and roasts chestnuts on it. Geese honk south overhead and everyone digs out a jumper. It's <kanji>autumn</kanji>.
秋.on: The scarecrow warms one straw foot, then the other, until his old <sound>shoe</sound> starts to smoke.
秋.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' sighs the farmer, warming his hands, then spots the barn <sound>key</sound> buried in a pile of leaves.

堂.meaning: On a raised mound of <part>soil</part> stands a building held in high <part>esteem</part>, with a sparkle on its roof and a great open door. Inside, a hundred people sit down to eat at one long table. It's the grand <kanji>hall</kanji>.
堂.on: In the kitchen, the cooks knead a mountain of bread <sound>dough</sound> to feed them all.

決.meaning: You can't choose which way to cross the river, so you load a <part>slingshot</part> and fire a stone through the <part>water drops</part> of the waterfall. Wherever it lands, that's where you'll go. Splash! The far bank. You <kanji>decide</kanji>.
決.on: Then you can't choose lunch either, so you fire a squirt of <sound>ketch</sound>up at the menu.
決.kun: On the far bank, the stone has landed right next to a lost <sound>key</sound>.

最.meaning: A greedy giant stands on tiptoe on the highest peak and reaches up to <part>take</part> the <part>sun</part> right out of the sky. Nobody has ever reached higher or grabbed more. It's the <kanji>utmost</kanji> anyone could do.
最.on: With the sun in his pocket, he cools off with a whole jug of <sound>ci</sound>der.
最.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le wants to go even higher: it stops, gulps, then scrambles to the very top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

祝.meaning: Your <part>big brother</part> passes his exams and climbs the <part>lamppost</part> in the square, waving his hat and singing. Streamers fly, friends cheer, someone pops a balloon. Tonight we all <kanji>celebrate</kanji>!
祝.on: From the top, he tosses a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be to everyone in the cheering crowd.
祝.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeal the little cousins, and '<sound>Wah</sound>!' they shout as he slides back down.

予.meaning: The night before the party, you slice every <part>pizza wedge</part>, wrap it and tick your list: <part>complete</part>. When the guests ring the bell there's nothing left to do. You did it all <kanji>beforehand</kanji>.
予.on: You even set out dessert early: a little pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt by every plate.
予.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>rah</sound>!' you cheer, loading a <sound>ca</sound>rp into the <sound>jee</sound>p the night before the fishing trip.

約.meaning: Two friends tie a <part>thread</part> between their wrists and share one <part>scoop</part> of ice cream to seal the deal. Whatever happens, they'll meet on this beach again next summer. It's a <kanji>promise</kanji>.
約.on: To mark the spot, they plant a spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca in the sand.
約.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' one sneezes, squeezing a yu<sound>zu</sound> so hard that it shrinks to the size of a pea.

優.meaning: A <part>coat hook</part> by the door holds a warm scarf for anyone who comes in heavy with <part>melancholy</part>. A friend wraps it round your shoulders, makes you tea and sits with you without a word. That's <kanji>tenderness</kanji>.
優.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn tiptoes in and rests its head gently in your lap.
優.kun: Your friend knits you a new scarf from soft <sound>ya</sound>rn and leaves a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines out for your cat.

怖.meaning: In the dark, a white <part>cloth</part> floats down the hall, swaying with no one inside it. Your <part>heartbeat</part> pounds in your ears, thump, thump, thump. It's a ghost, and it's <kanji>dreadful</kanji>.
怖.on: You dive under your <sound>fu</sound>ton and pull it right over your head.
怖.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala already hiding under there with you screams '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

悲.meaning: A cat licks a <part>fishbone</part> clean, then stares at the empty plate. No more fish. Its little <part>heart</part> sinks and its whiskers droop. Nothing in the world is quite so <kanji>sad</kanji>.
悲.on: It drags itself away like a dancer limping on a broken <sound>hee</sound>l.
悲.kun: A kind <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond takes pity and flips it a piece of <sound>na</sound>an.

紅.meaning: At her <part>workbench</part>, a tailor dips a <part>thread</part> into a pot of dye and pulls it out dripping, deep and dark like ripe cherries. She stitches a royal cloak with it. Every seam glows <kanji>crimson</kanji>.
紅.on: She tops it off with a hat shaped like a crimson ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
紅.kun: Sewing late in <sound>be</sound>d, she pricks her finger on the <sound>nee</sound>dle: one more red drop.

魚.meaning: A <part>boomerang</part> sails over a flooded <part>rice field</part>, knocks something silvery out of the water, and it lands flapping on the <part>hot coals</part> of your campfire. Sizzle! Caught and cooked in one throw: a <kanji>fish</kanji>.
魚.on: Beside the fish on the hot coals, a le<sound>ggy</sound> <sound>o</sound>ctopus curls up its arms and sizzles too.
魚.kun: Next you grill a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>ca</sound>rp and wrap them both in warm <sound>na</sound>an.

酸.meaning: A <part>stilt walker</part> steps carefully over a stick of <part>dynamite</part> that is leaking green, fizzing goo. Wherever it drips, the pavement hisses, smokes and melts away. Don't touch it: it's <kanji>acid</kanji>.
酸.on: One drop lands on your ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae, and it fizzes straight through the glass.
酸.kun: Even the <sound>su</sound>shi tastes sour now, as if it had been soaked in lemon juice.

源.meaning: Follow the stream uphill through the <part>meadow</part>, past cows and wildflowers, and you'll find <part>water drops</part> bubbling straight out of a crack in the ground. Every river starts somewhere: this is its <kanji>source</kanji>.
源.on: A hiker named <sound>Gen</sound> gets there first and guards the spring with a grin.
源.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat shares a <sound>na</sound>an with a <sound>mo</sound>le under a <sound>to</sound>tem pole beside the spring.

顔.meaning: A <part>stand</part> on the <part>cliff</part> top sells false <part>whiskers</part>. A <part>rubber duck</part> waddles up, tries a pair on and checks the mirror: eyes, beak and a bushy moustache. What a handsome <kanji>face</kanji>.
顔.on: Then it smears green <sound>gun</sound>k on its cheeks for face paint.
顔.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in the sea below looks up at the new face and gasps '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

結.meaning: Grandma takes a red <part>thread</part> and a charm for <part>good luck</part> and knots them round your wrist: once, twice, then a double bow. She pulls it tight. It won't come off until it wears away. That's how you <kanji>tie</kanji> a lucky knot.
結.on: At the wedding feast, a waiter ties a bib round your neck before the <sound>ketch</sound>up comes out.
結.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se ties a ribbon round a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi and gives it to you as a present.

婚.meaning: Under a bright <part>sun</part>, a <part>woman</part> walks between two families, and a whole <part>clan</part> lines up to throw petals. Two family names become one. It's a <kanji>marriage</kanji>.
婚.on: A giant <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down over the crowd, carrying the rings in its claws.

雪.meaning: The <part>rain</part> falls so cold that it freezes on the way down, and by morning the garden is white and soft. You grab a <part>rake</part> and drag it into heaps to build a fort. It's <kanji>snow</kanji>.
雪.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter dog bounds through the drifts, leaping and rolling.
雪.kun: The dog digs up a frozen <sound>yu</sound>zu and a lost car <sound>key</sound>.

速.meaning: A delivery boy lets go of a <part>bundle</part> of firewood at the top of a <part>ramp</part>. It bounces, spins and shoots down the street, past every cart and bike. Whoosh! That was <kanji>quick</kanji>.
速.on: On the way down it knocks a smelly <sound>sock</sound> off a washing line.
速.kun: Then it crashes into a little <sound>hu</sound>t full of <sound>ya</sound>rn, and balls go rolling everywhere.

快.meaning: A kid fires her <part>slingshot</part> at a grey cloud and it bursts into sunshine. Her <part>heartbeat</part> skips with joy, and she whistles all the way home. Nothing can spoil her mood today: she's <kanji>cheerful</kanji>.
快.on: Next she ties a <sound>ki</sound>te to the stone and fires it up into the blue.
快.kun: At home, a <sound>ko</sound>ala hugs a <sound>ko</sound>ala, a <sound>ro</sound>dent dances, and everyone shares the <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

疲.meaning: After a long day, a trapper drags a heavy <part>pelt</part> into a <part>leaky shed</part>, drips plopping on his head. He doesn't even bother to move. He flops onto the fur and lies there, soaked and <kanji>exhausted</kanji>.
疲.on: He kicks off his boots, and the <sound>hee</sound>l of one flies out through a hole in the roof.
疲.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes in the damp, too tired even to push a dripping <sound>ca</sound>rp off his chest.

妹.meaning: A little girl stands next to a grown <part>woman</part>, stretching on tiptoe to be just as tall. Is she as tall? <part>Not yet</part>. One day, she says. Until then, she's the <kanji>younger sister</kanji>.
妹.on: She keeps a box of pet <sound>mi</sound>ce under her bed and won't let anyone see them.
妹.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' she squeals as a lawn <sound>mow</sound>er chases her round a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

普.meaning: Under one <part>sun</part>, everyone stands side by side in a <part>row</part>: farmers, kings, cats and kids. The same light falls on each of them, no more and no less. It's the same for all: <kanji>universal</kanji>.
普.on: At bedtime, everyone in the row gets the same rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton.
普.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' they all sigh, each with a <sound>mu</sound>g of tea, as one big <sound>ne</sound>t of stars spreads over the whole world.

泉.meaning: Up in the hills, bright <part>white</part> foam bubbles out of a rock, and clear <part>water</part> tumbles over the stones below. Fill your cup: it's cold and sweet. You've found a <kanji>spring</kanji>.
泉.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands beside it, guarding it night and day.
泉.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' gasps a hiker, as a yu<sound>zu</sound> floats past and a <sound>mee</sound>rkat pops up to drink.

額.meaning: A <part>guest</part> arrives at the party with a <part>rubber duck</part> balanced on his head, just above his eyebrows. He bows hello and it slides off, so he sticks it back on with a lick. It lives on his <kanji>forehead</kanji>.
額.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese honks at the duck and pecks it off again.
額.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' giggles the host, and straps the duck back on with his <sound>tie</sound>.

乾.meaning: A <part>kebab</part> sits on the grill so long in the sun that it shrivels up like leather. A hungry dog comes to <part>beg</part> for it, takes one bite and spits it out. Not a drop of juice left: it's bone <kanji>dry</kanji>.
乾.on: Even the <sound>car</sound>nation in the vase on the table has gone crispy.
乾.kun: Down in the dried-up river, a <sound>ca</sound>rp flops on the cracked mud: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

皆.meaning: At the picnic there are <part>two spoons</part> and one big <part>white</part> bowl of pudding. Everyone crowds round, and the spoons go round and round, mouth to mouth, until the bowl is licked clean. Nobody is left out: there's some for <kanji>all</kanji>.
皆.on: After lunch they all fly one giant <sound>ki</sound>te together, everyone holding the same string.
皆.kun: Even the <sound>mee</sound>rkats get a share of the warm <sound>na</sound>an.
